claims.claim: The only explicitly market-related items in the window are a note that the Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 closed at record levels mid-window, and a report that UK inflation turned negative at -0.1%, the first negative reading in many years.

Corporate news in the window is limited to a single large announced merger (Charter Communications and Time Warner Cable, $55.1 billion) and a reported plan by Mediobanca to sell a 1.6% stake in Telecom Italia.

The final day of the window contains no macroeconomic, monetary, fiscal or systemic financial item; its contents are a Nigerian presidential inauguration, a volcanic eruption in Japan, attacks in Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, a Franco-German call on Russia over the Minsk ceasefire, a US criminal sentencing, a small Italian stake sale, and a rising MERS case count in South Korea.
A public-health item does escalate across the window, with South Korea confirming a third MERS case early and the count reaching twelve by the final day, but the absolute numbers remain very small.
The high-profile legal and geopolitical events in the window ",

The most prominent institutional story, the detention of six FIFA officials in Switzerland and the opening of Swiss criminal proceedings over World Cup awards, concerns a sports governing body rather than a listed entity or sovereign.

Conflict and disaster items are numerous but geographically dispersed and of a routine kind for the window: ISIS gains in Iraq and Syria, sectarian bombings in Saudi Arabia, flooding in Texas and Oklahoma, and a heat wave in India.

competing_explanation: The most defensible alternative reading is that a change in volatility conditions was seeded by the combination of equity indices printing record highs mid-window \u2014 a level from which realised volatility often rises without any news trigger \u2014 and the steady escalation of the South Korean MERS outbreak from three to twelve confirmed cases, which could plausibly transmit into Korean and regional travel/consumer assets. Both readings are weak: the record-high item is a description of calm rather than a shock, and twelve cases is a very small base on which to hang a regime change.
insufficient_evidence_reason: The window contains no item of clear and direct market significance: no central bank decision, no sovereign or credit event, no major macro data surprise beyond a single mild UK deflation print, no systemic financial institution news, and nothing on the flagged day that touches markets at all. The remaining items are conflict, disaster, criminal justice, sport and public-health stories that, individually and collectively, do not provide a credible transmission channel to a broad change in price and volatility conditions. On this evidence the flag is more consistent with noise or with a purely endogenous move from a low-volatility, record-high starting point than with any documented event.
